text:
Anya: quick heads-up — p99 on prod-serving spiked ~12% after last runtime change, alerts from canary too. wondering if our sampling/profiling is affecting numbers or if it really is a kernel/regression. attaching quick nsys snippet i ran on canary

Anya: command i used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=canary_trace --duration=30 --sample=none --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx
```

Anya: truncated timeline:
```
[GPU timeline] conv2d_kernel 0.0-5.0ms
[GPU timeline] matmul_kernel 5.1-8.7ms  (hot)
[KVcache] lookup_worker 8.9-9.3ms (cpu)
[GPU timeline] matmul_kernel 9.4-14.0ms  (hot, more execs)
```

Vikram: did you see increased matmul occupancy or a different kernel chosen? last rollout changed kernel-selection rule for seq<512 to prefer `matmul_fused_v2` if memory estimate < threshold.

Anya: yep looks like fused_v2 was picked. matmul_fused_v2 shows ~20% higher single-kernel time in this trace compared to matmul_baseline. unsure if it's density of ops or caching effects.

Maria: fwiw SRE saw small uptick in tail egress (redis miss rate) for kv-cache around same time; could be thrashing -> more cache misses -> longer KV lookup CPU time which cascades into different batching behavior.

Ken: if KV misses are increasing, batching heuristics might be degrading because requests elongated. do we have sampling vs full-trace bias? full nsys blocks and adds overhead — but sampling mode might hide a micro-regression.

Sam: quick numbers i ran locally:
- baseline (no profiler): p99 84ms
- nsys full (30s capture): p99 95ms
- nsys sampled (1/10 frames): p99 86ms
So full nsys adds ~13% tail, sampled much less.

Vikram: those numbers line up with my expectation. Full system tracing (nsys with kernel capture) serializes some threads and increases context switches on cpu-bound kv workers. We must treat full traces as debug-only on canary not prod.

Anya: agree. we need a safe-production profiling plan: minimal signal but low overhead to detect regressions and hotspots. proposed guardrails: 1) only sample 0.5-1% of requests cluster-aware 2) no nsys kernel capture in prod, prefer perfetto userspace + async kernel counters 3) cap trace duration to 2s per trace 4) auto-disable tracing for a node if p99 increases >5% within 10m of enabling

Maria: +1. also add rate-limited uploader and redaction of payloads. we should avoid blocking inference path for trace sync.

Ken: implementation notes: we can use eBPF uprobe/uretprobe for kv-cache lookup hotpaths to get call counts w/o heavy overhead. combine with random sampling of request IDs and tag samples with rollouts/canary flag.

Sam: rough pseudocode for sampling decision:
```
if rand() < 0.01 and node.is_canary and node.load < 0.8:
    enable_user_tracing(timeout=2s, kernel_capture=False)
else:
    no_trace
```

Vikram: for kernel selection debugging we should also store short per-request kernel name stacks (string list) and include top-1 kernel per step in trace metadata. cheap and helps correlate when fused_v2 gets picked.

Anya: +1. can we add a lightweight micro-tracer that records kernel_name -> exec_time histogram aggregated in memory and flushes every 30s? that avoids heavy traces and gives us quick drift signals.

Ken: yes — per-GPU circular buffer with atomic counters. flush via async writer to observability backend. small footprint.

Maria: operational guardrail: if sampling-based profiler notices >3x increase in matmul_fused_v2 median vs baseline, auto-create ticket + tag rollout and notify #incidents and oncall.

Sam: follow-up experiment proposal:
- deploy 0.75% sampling with userspace traces + kernel-name histogram to canary cluster for 2h
- compare per-kernel histograms vs last 24h baseline
- if matmul_fused_v2 median shifts >10% fail rollout

Anya: sounds good. i'll open a PR with implementation skeleton and add unit tests for random sampler and auto-disable logic. tagging @Vikram and @Ken to review.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: runtime/canary/2026-03-18T14:12Z -> canary-3 (sha: abcd1234) :rocket:

Vikram: thanks — small ask: add a `trace_enabled` field to request debug metadata so we can correlate incoming traces with client-level request context (customer tier, model).

Anya: will do. next steps: PR by EOD, run canary sampling experiment tomorrow morning, collect histograms. i'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
